clue.text: Rope in Constable, perhaps

John Constable is one example of an artist who works in oils

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word. John Constable was an English landscape artist, and a painter is also a boat's mooring rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a boat's mooring line, and an artist of whom Constable is an example.

clue.text: Soldier has a favourite form of defence

explanation.surface: A soldier with a preferred way of defending a position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A low protective wall along the edge of a roof or bridge is a defensive structure.

clue.text: To annoy, I dined wearing mink

parts.note: in means wearing, as in 'in a hat'
mink is a fur
ate means dined

explanation.surface: Wearing mink to dinner to annoy someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'I dined wearing mink'; the answer's order reads it as 'in fur I ate'.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrage someone is to make them very angry, a stronger version of annoying.

clue.text: Most of them join a Marine unit

explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a measure of heat used for gas in Britain.

clue.text: Bear up! Let off, being of good character

explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link. 'off' rearranges BEAR UP and LET.

clue.text: Scholars learned to 19

explanation.surface: Educated people have learned how to do the thing in clue 19.

explanation.definitionFit: Kneading muscles with the hands is exactly what a masseur does, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: So-called fashion house

indicators.note: so-called means as it is called or said, signalling a word that sounds like another

parts.note: manner means a style or fashion

explanation.definitionFit: A manor is a large country mansion.

clue.text: Disorganised pits overwhelmed by coal dust — it's a farce!

indicators.note: disorganised means put out of order

explanation.surface: Coal mines in chaos and full of dust: a ridiculous situation.

explanation.definitionFit: Broad physical comedy of a crude kind is a form of farce.

clue.text: One providing backing for a harpist

definitions.text: One providing backing for a harpist

parts.words: One providing backing for a harpist
parts.note: a person funding a theatre show, or one supporting heavenly harp music, a winged being with a harp

clue.text: Not the second worst challenge for climbers

indicators.note: not means the following letter is missing

parts.note: severest means worst, most severe

explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is a link. 'Not' removes S (second) from SEVEREST.

clue.text: Sack or fire

a gun with a grooved barrel is a firearm, the thing that fires

explanation.surface: An employer weighing whether to dismiss someone or let them go.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack a drawer is to search it roughly, and a long-barrelled gun is used to shoot.

clue.text: You need money to catch a star

parts.note: P stands for penny or pence, a coin of British money
to entangle something is to catch it in a snare or net

explanation.surface: Advice that only cash will bring a celebrity your way.

explanation.definitionFit: A five-pointed star drawn with a single unbroken line is the classic geometric figure of that name.

clue.text: Boundary lines of old concealed by man

rime is an old spelling of rhyme, verse lines

explanation.surface: A frontier marked by ancient lines hidden by a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed by' signals the container. Rime is the archaic spelling of rhyme, so 'lines of old' means old verse lines.

clue.text: Answer only five put in

clue.text: Walk or take public transport — parking's short

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle of public transport, here used as a verb
P is the short form, the sign, for parking

explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link word. P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to trudge a long way on foot, a heavy synonym of walk.

clue.text: Shame about a shift, say, in a family relationship

parts.note: a turn is a shift or session of work

clue.text: Talk softly when trapped by predator, a marsupial

explanation.surface: Soft talk while caught by a hunter: an image of a marsupial in danger.

explanation.definitionFit: The bandicoot is a small Australian pouched mammal, so it is an example of the group.

clue.text: Reputation — one I try to change

explanation.definitionFit: Notoriety is fame for something bad, so a kind of reputation.

clue.text: In full view, a man is passed

parts.note: overt means open, in full view

explanation.surface: A man was overtaken in full view of the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link.

clue.text: Medical attention for people beginning to tremble after feast

clue.text: Vessel put vehicle on a road

parts.note: a tank is an armoured vehicle

explanation.surface: Putting a vehicle on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put' and 'on' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankard is a drinking mug, a kind of vessel for beer.

clue.text: Work on poverty, we hear

clue.text: Awful doctor supervising a deed that's awful

clue.text: Someone very close — surely not!

clue.text: It's highly important to have half a dozen soldiers left

clue.text: Measure the depth of water in well
